[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on cyclic AMP as an intracellular messenger and on the cells that depend on it. Two calcium/calmodulin-stimulated adenylate cyclases, ADCY1 and ADCY8, generate cAMP in neurons in response to calcium entry, coupling synaptic activity to kinase signalling and long-term potentiation; the serotonin receptor HTR6 and a G protein gamma subunit sit upstream of the same second-messenger route, while CAMK2N1 restrains calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II and so tunes the calcium arm of the response.

reading_2.theme: cAMP-PKA second-messenger signalling in neurons

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release.

reading_2.theme: Ubiquitin-proteasome system and deubiquitination

reading_2.theme: Deoxyribonucleotide pool metabolism: breakdown, salvage and synthesis

reading_2.theme: Vitamin D, phosphate and vitamin K bone-mineral regulation

reading_2.theme: MicroRNA control of fibrosis and wound-healing repair

reading_2.theme: Centrosome positioning and mitotic spindle orientation
reading_2.core_role: The shared pathways are centrosome positioning and microtubule nucleation/anchoring at the MTOC and cortex, framed as the basis for spindle positioning and asymmetric division in mitosis.
